meta.name: offensive-lorawan-sub-ghz
meta.description: LoRaWAN and sub-GHz (433 / 868 / 915 MHz) attack methodology — LoRaWAN ABP/OTAA join attack, network/session key reuse, frame counter replay, downlink injection on TTN/Helium-style networks, sub-GHz protocol replay (KeeLoq garage doors, fixed-code remotes, TPMS spoofing, smart plug telemetry), HackRF / RTL-SDR / Flipper Zero workflows, signal analysis with Inspectrum / Universal Radio Hacker, and reconstruction of proprietary packet formats. Use for LoRaWAN deployments (smart cities, asset tracking, industrial telemetry), or any wireless device using the unlicensed 433/868/915 MHz bands (garage openers, doorbells, IoT sensors, RC equipment).

howto.what_en: Claude will guide you through attacking LoRaWAN networks and sub-GHz wireless devices, including signal capture, key cracking, and packet replay.
howto.when_en: Triggered when you need to test security of LoRaWAN smart city, asset tracking, or other IoT devices, as well as sub-GHz devices like garage doors, doorbells, and sensors operating in 433/868/915 MHz bands.

say_en.text: How to capture and replay a fixed-code remote signal?
say_en.note: Claude will provide steps using Flipper Zero or HackRF.

say_en.text: How to perform a join attack on LoRaWAN OTAA devices?
say_en.note: Claude will explain capturing Join-Request and decrypting with AppKey.

say_en.text: How to auto-decode 433MHz devices with rtl_433?
say_en.note: Claude will give rtl_433 commands and common protocol identification.
